svg.title: How my apps run — architecture overview
svg.desc: Users reach Arbeitseule over HTTPS on one AWS server behind Caddy. Cloudflare provides DNS, bot protection, mail routing and a login gate with a tunnel to the internal control center. GitHub holds the code, tests every pull request and deploys after approval. Backups go to S3, alarms come from CloudWatch.
svg.text: Architecture overview · Frank David Lee · November 2026
EC2 serverone small ARM instance · Ubuntu

g.text: AI coding agent · writes code as pull requests
login gate and tunnel in front
reads PRs and runs · starts approved deploy

svg.text: Users open arbeitseule.com: DNS at Cloudflare, HTTPS goes straight to the server.
Caddy terminates TLS and forwards to the apps, which listen on localhost only.
Arbeitseule calls the Claude API and job board APIs — never with a user's name or e-mail.
Outbound mail via Amazon SES (SPF, DKIM, DMARC); inbound mail via Cloudflare to Gmail.
The operator signs in through Cloudflare Access; an outbound tunnel reaches the control center.
The control center reads GitHub and can start exactly one action: an approved production deploy.
Claude Code opens pull requests, GitHub Actions tests them, a deploy needs my approval.
Daily encrypted backups to S3; CloudWatch raises an alarm if health or backups fail.
